newsitem.title: USA: U.S. domestic crude diffs weaken on slow demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. domestic crude diffs weaken on slow demand.

text.p: U.S. domestic grades held a softer tone late Wednesday amid sluggish refiner interest and after finding limited support from overall crude stock draws.
A rally in heating oil was also offset by perception that runs would be reduced for autumn turnarounds, traders said.
October West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was 45 cents up on Tuesday at $23.80-90 a barrel, garnering support from reports the U.S. had deployed more troops in the Middle East.
But price backwardation remained volatile around 40 cents, and domestic grade differentials were broadly weaker, suggesting a not-so-firm prompt outlook.
Crude inventory builds in the Gulf Coast of 2.3 million barrels dragged on Gulf Coast grades, especially now that the Atlantic arbitrage threatened to bring in more supplies.
A handful of grades traded at weaker price levels with end users staying on the sides waiting for volatility to subside.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James traded at WTI plus 18 to 22 cents, down about 10 cents from Tuesday.
WTI/Midland also shrivalled to WTI parity, down six cents, with Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire moving at minus 5/10 cents, off from plus 2/3 cents recently.
Heavy, sour grades also faced downward pressure.
West Texas Sour/Midland traded at a $1.24 discount to WTI, down 7-8 cts from trades seen Tuesday at minus $1.17-$1.19.
Eugene Island skidded down to WTI minus $1.30, down further from the morning's minus $1.17 and $1.18 levels.
Short covering for pipeline scheduling in the days ahead, following the expiry of NYMEX OCt crude on Friday, was seen providing only minimal support.
No supply shortage and upcoming refinery turnarounds placed a lid on differentials, traders said.
